expensesApp.froms module

Django Forms Module for Expense Tracking Application.

This module contains all form classes used for data input and validation in the expense tracking system.

Forms Included:

  • categoryForm: ModelForm for creating/editing expense categories

  • ExpenseForm: ModelForm for recording expense amounts

  • CycleForm: Standard Form for budget cycle configuration

Each form handles specific validation rules and user input processing for different parts of the application.

class expensesApp.froms.categoryForm(data=None, files=None, auto_id='id_%s', prefix=None, initial=None, error_class=<class 'django.forms.utils.ErrorList'>, label_suffix=None, empty_permitted=False, instance=None, use_required_attribute=None, renderer=None)[source]

Bases: ModelForm

Form for creating and editing expense categories.

This ModelForm handles category creation with automatic user assignment. The ‘user’ field is excluded because it’s set automatically from the request object in the view, preventing users from assigning categories to other users.

Features:

  • Automatic user assignment in view layer

  • Supports icon image upload

  • Enforces unique category names per user

Example

>>> form = categoryForm(request.POST, request.FILES)
>>> if form.is_valid():
...     category = form.save(commit=False)
...     category.user = request.user
...     category.save()

Note

The user field is explicitly excluded to prevent tampering. Always use commit=False and assign the user from request.user.

class expensesApp.froms.ExpenseForm(data=None, files=None, auto_id='id_%s', prefix=None, initial=None, error_class=<class 'django.forms.utils.ErrorList'>, label_suffix=None, empty_permitted=False, instance=None, use_required_attribute=None, renderer=None)[source]

Bases: ModelForm

Form for creating new expense transactions.

A simplified ModelForm that only captures the expense amount. Other fields (user, cycle, category, timestamp) are set automatically by the view based on the current request context and user selections.

Why only amount?:

  • Category is selected separately in the template dropdown

  • User comes from request.user

  • Cycle comes from active budget cycle

  • Timestamp is auto-set by the model

Example

>>> form = ExpenseForm(request.POST)
>>> if form.is_valid():
...     expense = form.save(commit=False)
...     expense.user = request.user
...     expense.category = selected_category
...     expense.cycle = active_cycle
...     expense.save()

Note

Only the ‘amount’ field is exposed to users. All other fields are populated automatically in the view based on the current session and user selections.

Bases: Form

Form for creating and updating budget spending cycles.

A standard Django Form (not a ModelForm) that collects budget cycle parameters from the user. This form is used to initialize or modify the user’s spending cycle, with start/end dates calculated server-side.

Why not a ModelForm?:

  • start_date and end_date are calculated, not user input

  • is_active is set programmatically

  • Only allowance and duration are needed from users

Form Fields:

total_allowance (Decimal): User’s total budget for the cycle duration_days (Integer): Length of the budget cycle in days

Validation Rules:

  • total_allowance: Minimum $0.01, maximum 10 digits with 2 decimal places

  • duration_days: Between 1 and 365 days (inclusive)

Example

>>> form = CycleForm(request.POST)
>>> if form.is_valid():
...     allowance = form.cleaned_data['total_allowance']
...     days = form.cleaned_data['duration_days']
...     start_date = timezone.now().date()
...     end_date = start_date + timedelta(days=days - 1)
...     Cycle.objects.create(
...         user=request.user,
...         total_allowance=allowance,
...         start_date=start_date,
...         end_date=end_date,
...         is_active=True
...     )

Note

This is a standard Form, not a ModelForm, because the Cycle model contains calculated fields (start_date, end_date) that are derived from these inputs rather than collected directly from users. The one-year maximum (365 days) encourages regular budget reviews.

total_allowance

Total budget amount for the spending cycle.

This is the maximum amount the user can spend during the budget cycle.

Validation Rules:

  • Maximum 10 digits total (e.g., 9,999,999.99)

  • Maximum 2 decimal places (cents precision)

  • Minimum value: $0.01 (prevents zero or negative budgets)

  • Must be a positive decimal number

Example valid values:

  • 500.00 (Five hundred dollars)

  • 1000.50 (One thousand dollars and fifty cents)

  • 250.75 (Two hundred fifty dollars and seventy-five cents)

Example invalid values:

  • 0.00 (Too low - must be at least $0.01)

  • -50.00 (Negative not allowed)

  • 1000.123 (Too many decimal places)

The value is stored as Decimal to maintain precise monetary calculations without floating-point errors.

base_fields = {'duration_days': <django.forms.fields.IntegerField object>, 'total_allowance': <django.forms.fields.DecimalField object>}
declared_fields = {'duration_days': <django.forms.fields.IntegerField object>, 'total_allowance': <django.forms.fields.DecimalField object>}
property media

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

duration_days

Length of the budget cycle in days.

Determines how long the budget cycle will last from the start date. The system automatically calculates the end date based on this value.

Validation Rules:

  • Minimum: 1 day (single day cycle - for daily budgeting)

  • Maximum: 365 days (one year - annual budget cycle)

  • Must be a positive integer

How end date is calculated:

start_date = current date (when form is submitted) end_date = start_date + (duration_days - 1)

Examples

  • duration_days = 1 → Same day cycle (ends today)

  • duration_days = 7 → One week cycle

  • duration_days = 30 → Approximately one month cycle

  • duration_days = 365 → One year cycle

Why limit to 365 days?:

  • Encourages regular budget reviews

  • Prevents excessively long cycles

  • Aligns with annual financial planning

  • Maintains data freshness

Note

Includes validation to prevent cycles longer than one year to ensure regular budget reviews and accurate tracking. Users can create a new cycle after the previous one ends.

expensesApp.models module

Expenses App Models Module.

This module defines the database models for the expense tracking system:

Models Included:

  • Cycle: Represents budget periods with spending limits and date ranges

  • Category: Organizes expenses by type for better tracking

  • Expense: Records individual spending transactions

Each model includes appropriate fields, relationships, and methods for managing personal finance data with user-specific filtering.

class expensesApp.models.Cycle(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

Represents a budget cycle for a user’s expense tracking period.

A cycle defines the timeframe during which expenses are tracked against a total allowance. Each user has one active cycle at a time, which is used to calculate spending limits and progress.

user

One-to-one relationship with userRegistration model. Each user can have only one active cycle at a time.

start_date

Starting date of the budget cycle. All expenses after this date belong to this cycle.

end_date

Ending date of the budget cycle. Expenses after this date are not counted in this cycle.

total_allowance

Maximum spending amount allowed for this cycle. Used to calculate remaining budget and progress.

is_active

Flag indicating if this is the current active cycle. Only one cycle can be active per user at any time.

Relationships:

  • OneToOne with userRegistration (each user has one cycle at a time)

  • One-to-Many with Expense (a cycle can have many expenses)

Example

>>> cycle = Cycle.objects.create(
...     user=user,
...     start_date=date(2024, 1, 1),
...     end_date=date(2024, 1, 31),
...     total_allowance=1000.00,
...     is_active=True
... )
>>> print(cycle)
'john_doe 2024-01-01----2024-01-31'

Note

Only one cycle should be active per user at any given time. The is_active flag is managed by the setCycle view.

user

One-to-one relationship to the user who owns this budget cycle.

Field Details:

  • Type: OneToOneField (each user has exactly one cycle at a time)

  • Related Model: userRegistration (custom user model)

  • Nullable: Yes (allows cycles without user association for testing)

  • Blank: Yes (can be empty in forms)

  • On Delete: CASCADE - if user is deleted, their cycle is also deleted

Why OneToOne?:

Users should only have ONE active budget cycle at a time. This enforces that constraint at the database level.

start_date

Starting date of the budget cycle.

Field Details:

  • Type: DateField (stores year, month, day)

  • Default: Current date/time when cycle is created

  • Timezone: Uses Django’s timezone settings

Usage:

Expenses with timestamp >= start_date belong to this cycle. Used to calculate days remaining and daily spending limits.

Example: 2024-01-01 (January 1, 2024)

end_date

Ending date of the budget cycle.

Field Details:

  • Type: DateField (stores year, month, day)

  • Default: Current date/time when cycle is created

  • Must be >= start_date (enforced in view logic)

Usage:

Expenses with timestamp <= end_date belong to this cycle. Used with start_date to calculate total cycle duration. After this date, the cycle is considered ‘ended’.

Example: 2024-01-31 (January 31, 2024)

total_allowance

Total spending budget for the cycle.

Field Details:

  • Type: DecimalField (precision for monetary values)

  • Max Digits: 10 (up to 99,999,999.99)

  • Decimal Places: 2 (cents precision)

  • Required: Yes (must be provided)

Usage:

  • Compared against total_expenses to track progress

  • Used to calculate remaining budget

  • Determines safe daily spending limits

Calculations:

remaining_budget = total_allowance - total_spent progress_percent = (total_spent / total_allowance) * 100 safe_daily_limit = remaining_budget / days_remaining

Example: 1000.00 (One thousand dollars)

is_active

Flag indicating if this is the user’s active budget cycle.

Field Details:

  • Type: BooleanField (True/False)

  • Default: True (new cycles start as active)

Behavior:

  • Only ONE cycle per user should have is_active=True

  • Active cycle is used for current expense tracking

  • Inactive cycles are kept for historical data

  • Users can only add expenses to the active cycle

State Transitions:

  • New cycle created → is_active = True

  • Cycle ends (past end_date) → set is_active = False

  • User creates new cycle → old cycle becomes inactive

Example

>>> # Deactivate old cycle
>>> old_cycle.is_active = False
>>> old_cycle.save()
>>> # Create new active cycle
>>> new_cycle = Cycle.objects.create(...)  # is_active=True by default

class expensesApp.models.Category(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

Represents an expense category for organizing spending.

Categories allow users to group their expenses by type (e.g., Food, Transport, Entertainment, Utilities). Each category is unique per user, meaning two users can have a “Food” category, but one user cannot have duplicate category names.

user

Foreign key to userRegistration (owner of the category)

name

Display name of the category (required, max 100 chars)

icon

Optional image icon for visual representation

Constraints:

  • unique_together = [‘user’, ‘name’]: Prevents duplicate category names per user

Example

>>> category = Category.objects.create(
...     user=user,
...     name="Groceries",
...     icon="groceries.png"
... )
>>> print(category)
'Groceries'

Note

Categories are user-specific. Each user has their own set of categories independent of other users.

user

Foreign key to the user who owns this category.

Field Details:

  • Type: ForeignKey (many categories can belong to one user)

  • Related Model: userRegistration (custom user model)

  • Nullable: Yes (allows categories without user for testing)

  • Blank: Yes (can be empty in forms)

  • On Delete: CASCADE - if user is deleted, their categories are deleted

Why ForeignKey?:

Users can have multiple categories, but each category belongs to exactly one user. This is a standard one-to-many relationship.

Example

User “john” can have categories: Food, Transport, Entertainment User “jane” can have categories: Food, Rent, Utilities (Both can have “Food” - it’s independent per user)

name

Display name of the expense category.

Field Details:

  • Type: CharField (string/text)

  • Max Length: 100 characters

  • Required: Yes (cannot be null or blank)

  • Unique together with user field

Validation:

  • Must be unique per user (enforced by Meta.unique_together)

  • Maximum 100 characters

  • Cannot be empty string

Examples

  • “Food & Dining”

  • “Transportation”

  • “Rent/Mortgage”

  • “Utilities”

  • “Entertainment”

  • “Healthcare”

  • “Shopping”

  • “Education”

Note

Category names should be descriptive enough to help users understand what type of expenses belong in each category.

icon

Optional icon image for visual category representation.

Field Details:

  • Type: ImageField (handles image upload and storage)

  • Required: No (null=True, blank=True)

  • Upload To: Root of MEDIA_ROOT (empty string = MEDIA_ROOT)

  • Default: ‘anchor.png’ (default icon if none provided)

Supported Formats:

  • PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF (depends on Pillow library)

File Storage:

  • Uploads to: MEDIA_ROOT / (filename)

  • URL accessible at: MEDIA_URL / (filename)

  • Default icon: static/images/anchor.png

Usage in Templates:

<img src=”{{ category.icon.url }}” alt=”{{ category.name }}”>

Example

User uploads ‘food_icon.png’ → stored at MEDIA_ROOT/food_icon.png URL: /images/food_icon.png

Note

For production, ensure MEDIA_ROOT and MEDIA_URL are properly configured and files are served by your web server.

class expensesApp.models.Expense(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

Represents a financial expense transaction.

Records individual spending entries linked to a specific budget cycle and category. Automatically timestamps each expense when created. Ordered by most recent first for easy review.

user

Foreign key to userRegistration (person who made the expense)

cycle

Foreign key to Cycle (budget period this expense belongs to)

category

Foreign key to Category (expense type classification)

amount

Monetary value of the expense (supports up to 20 digits)

time_stamp

Auto-recorded datetime when expense was created

Default Ordering:

  • Most recent expenses first (newest at top)

Example

>>> expense = Expense.objects.create(
...     user=user,
...     cycle=current_cycle,
...     category=food_category,
...     amount=45.50
... )
>>> print(expense)
'2024-01-15 14:30:00+00:00--Groceries'

Note

The time_stamp is automatically set when the expense is created and cannot be manually modified by users.

user_id
user

Foreign key to the user who made this expense.

Field Details:

  • Type: ForeignKey (many expenses can belong to one user)

  • Related Model: userRegistration (custom user model)

  • Nullable: Yes (allows testing without user)

  • On Delete: CASCADE - if user is deleted, their expenses are deleted

Purpose:

  • Associates expense with the correct user

  • Enables user-specific expense filtering

  • Ensures users only see their own expenses

  • Used for user-specific budget calculations

Security:

  • Always filter expenses by request.user in views

  • Never show expenses of other users

cycle

Foreign key to the budget cycle this expense belongs to.

Field Details:

  • Type: ForeignKey (many expenses can belong to one cycle)

  • Related Model: Cycle (budget period)

  • Required: Yes (must be specified)

  • On Delete: CASCADE - if cycle is deleted, its expenses are deleted

Purpose:

  • Associates expense with specific budget period

  • Enables cycle-specific budget calculations

  • Tracks which cycle’s allowance is being used

Important

Each expense must belong to an active cycle. Users cannot add expenses without an active budget cycle. The setCycle view enforces this requirement.

category

Foreign key to the category classifying this expense.

Field Details:

  • Type: ForeignKey (many expenses can belong to one category)

  • Related Model: Category (expense classification)

  • Required: Yes (must be specified)

  • On Delete: CASCADE - if category is deleted, its expenses are deleted

Purpose:

  • Categorizes expenses for reporting

  • Enables category-based spending analysis

  • Powers the spending insights charts

Example Categories:

  • Food (groceries, restaurants)

  • Transport (gas, public transit, taxis)

  • Entertainment (movies, games, hobbies)

  • Utilities (electricity, water, internet)

Note

When a category is deleted, all expenses in that category are also deleted (CASCADE behavior). Warn users before deletion.

amount

Monetary amount of the expense transaction.

Field Details:

  • Type: DecimalField (precision for monetary values)

  • Max Digits: 20 (extremely large values - for enterprise use)

  • Decimal Places: 2 (cents precision)

  • Required: Yes (must be provided)

Validation:

  • Must be positive number (enforced in form and view)

  • Cannot be zero or negative (business logic)

  • Precision handles most real-world expenses

Examples

  • 4.99 (Coffee)

  • 45.50 (Groceries)

  • 1200.00 (Rent)

  • 25000.00 (Car purchase)

Usage in Calculations:

  • total_spent = SUM(amount) where user=X and cycle=Y

  • remaining_budget = total_allowance - total_spent

  • today_spent = SUM(amount) where date=today

Note

Stored as Decimal to maintain precise monetary calculations without floating-point rounding errors. Always use Decimal for financial data, never float!

time_stamp

Timestamp when the expense was created/recorded.

Field Details:

  • Type: DateTimeField (stores date and time)

  • Auto-Add: automatically set to current time on creation

  • Cannot be manually edited

  • Includes timezone information (if USE_TZ=True)

Automatic Behavior:

  • Set when expense object is first saved

  • Never changes on subsequent updates

  • Uses Django’s timezone.now()

Usage:

  • Ordering expenses (newest first)

  • Daily spending calculations

  • Date-range filtering

  • Spending patterns analysis

  • Time-based reports

Example values:

  • 2024-01-15 14:30:00+00:00 (January 15, 2024 at 2:30 PM UTC)

  • 2024-01-20 09:15:22+00:00 (January 20, 2024 at 9:15 AM UTC)

Note

This timestamp reflects when the expense was entered, not necessarily when the purchase occurred. For precise purchase date tracking, consider adding a separate purchase_date field if needed in the future.

expensesApp.tests module

expensesApp.urls module

Expenses App URL Configuration.

This module defines all URL patterns for the expense tracking functionality including expense management, category operations, budget cycle setup, and spending analytics.

URL Patterns Overview:

  • Expense Management: Add expenses, view all expenses

  • Category Management: Create, edit, delete, list categories

  • Budget Cycle: Set up initial budget cycle

  • Analytics: Visual spending insights and charts

All URLs are namespaced under the expenses app and can be referenced using the ‘name’ attribute in templates and views.

expensesApp.urls.urlpatterns = [<URLPattern 'addExpense/' [name='addExpense']>, <URLPattern 'addcategory/' [name='addCategory']>, <URLPattern 'showAllexpenses/' [name='dislpayExpenses']>, <URLPattern 'categories/' [name='category_list']>, <URLPattern 'categories/edit/<int:category_id>/' [name='edit_category']>, <URLPattern 'categories/delete/<int:category_id>/' [name='delete_category']>, <URLPattern 'setCycle/' [name='setCycle']>, <URLPattern 'insights/' [name='spendingInsights']>]

URL Name Reference for Templates and Views:

Expense Operations:

{% url ‘addExpense’ %} - Add new expense {% url ‘dislpayExpenses’ %} - View all expenses (note typo)

Category Operations:

{% url ‘addCategory’ %} - Create new category {% url ‘category_list’ %} - List all categories {% url ‘edit_category’ category.id %} - Edit specific category {% url ‘delete_category’ category.id %} - Delete specific category

Budget Cycle:

{% url ‘setCycle’ %} - Setup budget cycle

Analytics:

{% url ‘spendingInsights’ %} - View spending charts

Usage in Views (reverse() function):

from django.urls import reverse url = reverse(‘addExpense’) url = reverse(‘edit_category’, args=[category_id]) url = reverse(‘category_list’)

Usage in Redirects:

from django.shortcuts import redirect return redirect(‘addExpense’) return redirect(‘category_list’)

expensesApp.views module

Expenses App Views Module.

This module contains all view functions for the expense tracking application, including expense management, category operations, budget cycle setup, and spending analytics.

All views are protected by @login_required decorator, ensuring only authenticated users can access expense tracking functionality.

Views Included:

  • addExpense: Handle expense creation with budget validation

  • addCategory: Create new expense categories

  • displayAllexpenses: Show all user expenses

  • setCycle: Initialize or update budget cycle

  • spendingInsights: Generate spending analytics and charts

  • category_list: Display all user categories

  • edit_category: Modify existing categories

  • delete_category: Remove categories and associated expenses

expensesApp.views.addExpense(request)[source]

Handle expense creation with comprehensive budget validation.

This view processes expense form submissions, validates against the user’s active budget cycle, and provides real-time warnings for:

  • Budget threshold alerts (80% and 100% usage)

  • Daily safe spending limit violations

Features:

  • Pre-save validation and checks

  • Budget percentage calculations (before and after save)

  • Threshold alerts for budget milestones

  • Daily spending limit warnings

Parameters:

request – HTTP request object containing POST data with expense amount and selected category

Returns:

Rendered addExpense.html template with form and categories context

Alert Conditions:

  • 100% Budget: Error message when budget is exhausted

  • 80% Budget: Warning message when nearing limit

  • Daily Limit: Warning when daily spending exceeds safe limit

Process Flow:

  1. GET: Display empty expense form with user’s categories

  2. POST: Process expense submission a. Validate form and category existence b. Check for active budget cycle c. Calculate pre-save budget percentage d. Save expense e. Calculate post-save budget percentage f. Trigger alerts based on thresholds g. Check daily spending limit h. Display appropriate success/error messages

Example

POST request with:

amount: 50.00 categories: Food

Result: Expense saved, budget alerts shown if thresholds crossed

expensesApp.views.addCategory(request)[source]

Create a new expense category for the authenticated user.

Allows users to define custom categories for organizing their expenses. Each category is user-specific and includes an optional icon image.

Parameters:

request – HTTP request object containing POST data with category name and optional icon file upload

Returns:

Rendered addCategory.html template with category form

Process:

GET: Display empty category form POST: Process category creation

  • Validate form data

  • Assign user to category

  • Save to database

  • Display success/error messages

Validation:

  • Category name must be unique per user

  • Name cannot be empty

  • Icon file must be valid image format

Messages:

Success: ‘category added successfully!’ Error: ‘category already exist’ (if duplicate name)

Example

POST request with:

name: “Transportation” icon: bus.png (optional)

Result: New category created for the user

Display all categories belonging to the authenticated user.

Retrieves and displays alphabetically ordered list of user’s expense categories for management purposes.

Parameters:

request – HTTP request object from authenticated user

Returns:

Rendered category_list.html template with categories context

Context Variables:

categories: QuerySet of Category objects ordered alphabetically by name

Template Usage:
{% for category in categories %}

{{ category.name }} <img src=”{{ category.icon.url }}”> <a href=”{% url ‘edit_category’ category.id %}”>Edit</a> <a href=”{% url ‘delete_category’ category.id %}”>Delete</a>

{% endfor %}

Example

expensesApp.views.edit_category(request, category_id)[source]

Edit an existing expense category.

Allows users to modify category name and/or icon image. Ensures the category belongs to the requesting user for security.

Parameters:

  • request – HTTP request object containing POST data for updates

  • category_id – Primary key of the category to edit (from URL)

Returns:

Rendered edit_category.html with pre-filled form POST (success): Redirect to category_list with success message POST (invalid): Re-render form with error messages

Return type:

GET

Security:

  • Verifies category belongs to current user

  • Prevents editing other users’ categories

Messages:

Success: ‘Category “{name}” updated successfully!’ Error: ‘Please correct the errors below’

Example

POST /categories/edit/5/ with:

name: “Groceries” (updated from “Food”) icon: new_icon.png

Result: Category updated and user redirected to category list

expensesApp.views.delete_category(request, category_id)[source]

Delete an existing expense category.

Removes a category from the user’s account. ⚠️ WARNING: All expenses associated with this category will also be deleted due to CASCADE relationship in the database model.

Parameters:

  • request – HTTP request object (POST confirms deletion)

  • category_id – Primary key of the category to delete (from URL)

Returns:

Rendered delete_category.html with confirmation prompt POST: Redirect to category_list with success message after deletion

Return type:

GET

Security:

  • Verifies category belongs to current user

  • Requires POST confirmation for deletion

Messages:

Success: ‘Category “{name}” deleted successfully!’

Warning

Uses CASCADE delete - all expenses in this category will be removed! The confirmation page should display this warning to users.

Example

POST /categories/delete/5/ Deletes category with id=5 and all related expenses

Returns:

Rendered Expenses.html template with all user expenses in context

expenses: QuerySet of Expense objects for the current user

Ordered by time_stamp descending (newest first)

{{ expense.time_stamp }} - {{ expense.category.name }}: ${{ expense.amount }}

{% endfor %}

expensesApp.views.setCycle(request)[source]

Create or update user’s budget spending cycle (User Story 1).

Allows students to input their total cash allowance and cycle duration. Automatically calculates start date, end date, and displays current daily spending limit based on remaining budget.

Parameters:

request – HTTP request object containing POST data with: total_allowance: Total budget for the cycle (min $0.01) duration_days: Number of days the cycle should last (1-365)

Returns:

form: CycleForm for user input existing_cycle: Current cycle if exists (for display) preview_daily_limit: Calculated safe daily spending amount

Return type:

Rendered setCycle.html template with

Process:
GET Request:

  1. Check for existing cycle

  2. Pre-fill form if cycle exists

  3. Calculate preview daily limit

  4. Display form with current/pre-filled values

POST Request:

  1. Validate form data

  2. Calculate start_date = today

  3. Calculate end_date = start_date + duration_days - 1

  4. Create new cycle OR update existing

  5. Set is_active = True (deactivates any previous cycle)

  6. Redirect to home page with success message

Formula:

start_date = current date end_date = start_date + duration_days - 1 days_remaining = max((end_date - today).days + 1, 1) remaining_budget = total_allowance - total_spent daily_safe_limit = remaining_budget / days_remaining

Example

POST request with:

total_allowance: 1000.00 duration_days: 30

Creates cycle: Jan 1 - Jan 30 with $1000 budget

Note

First-time users are redirected here after registration due to is_first_login flag in user model.

expensesApp.views.spendingInsights(request)[source]

Generate visual spending breakdown for user’s active budget cycle (User Story 3).

Creates a server-side computed horizontal bar chart showing expenses grouped by category with percentages. Uses pure CSS for visualization with no JavaScript required.

Parameters:

request – HTTP request object from authenticated user

Returns:

cycle: Active budget cycle total_spent: Sum of all expenses in current cycle category_rows: List of category spending breakdowns

Return type:

Rendered spendingInsights.html template with

Category Row Structure:

  • name: Category name (string)

  • amount: Total spent in category (Decimal)

  • percentage: Percentage of total budget (float)

  • color: Assigned color for visualization (hex code)

Process:

  1. Retrieve active cycle for current user

  2. Calculate total spent across all categories

  3. Group expenses by category using values() and annotate()

  4. Sum amounts per category

  5. Order by highest spending first

  6. Calculate percentage for each category

  7. Assign distinct colors from predefined palette

  8. Prepare data for CSS bar chart rendering

Color Palette (10 colors):

indigo, amber, emerald, red, blue, purple, pink, teal, orange, lime

Example Output:
category_rows = [

{‘name’: ‘Food’, ‘amount’: 350.00, ‘percentage’: 35.0, ‘color’: ‘#6366f1’}, {‘name’: ‘Transport’, ‘amount’: 150.00, ‘percentage’: 15.0, ‘color’: ‘#f59e0b’}, {‘name’: ‘Entertainment’, ‘amount’: 100.00, ‘percentage’: 10.0, ‘color’: ‘#10b981’}

]

Note

All calculations are server-side to ensure data accuracy and prevent manipulation. Charts render without external JavaScript libraries for improved performance.
